title: Mukai-Gram universality of normalized descendent and tangent-Chern integrals for fine proper stable-sheaf moduli on K3 surfaces of dimension greater than two
author: Georg Oberdieck
work: Universality of Descendent Integrals over Moduli Spaces of Stable Sheaves on K3 Surfaces
source_version: Official SIGMA 18 (2022) article 076, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2022.076; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof handles degenerate Mukai-Gram configurations by a genuine vanishing argument for isotropic radical insertions, then repeatedly removes those directions without changing the integrals. It constructs an isometry for the resulting nondegenerate spans and transports the normalized descendent classes and tangent Chern classes through Markman operators. The radical reduction is essential because an equality of Gram matrices alone does not identify arbitrary degenerate configurations by an isometry.

source_check.note: Complete author Theorem2.9 route: normalized universal class uv and B_i definitions, full Lemma2.7, isotropic vanishing Proposition2.10 (both author proofs), degenerate-span reduction2.11, elementary Gram lemmas2.12–2.13 and the final integral comparison. M=M_H(v) is the smooth proper fine moduli space for a positive primitive Mukai vector, v-generic polarization and a universal sheaf, with dim(M)=v.v+2>2. The selected P is a rational polynomial in normalized B_i(x_j) and tangent Chern classes and x_j belong to the Mukai lattice; its integral depends only on P and the full Gram matrix of v,x_j. Markman operator Theorem2.4 is genuinely established prior background with the source coefficient-extension explanation preserved. Twisted-universal, Bridgeland and dimension-two extensions are not selected; no separate Hilbert-reconstruction or Segre-Verlinde consequence is counted. Source approval supplied only by exact frozen root input; no new source/difficulty decision or mathematical referee.
